## Table 4 — Robustness summary

| Error source | old | average | new | Best fit | Risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| sigma 0.10 to 0.15 (W) | x1.41 | x1.52 | x1.48 | — | — |
| AR(1) rho = 0.4 (W) | x1.48 | x1.49 | x1.44 | — | — |
| k_b = -0.4 (D) | -0.66 | -1.53 | -1.58 | 0.996 | Spearman 0.975; top-6 0.50 / 1.00 |
| k_b = -0.6 (D) | +0.56 | +1.41 | +1.49 | 0.997 | Spearman 0.934; top-6 0.50 / 0.71 |
| sensor bias, max over arms (D) | +3.87 | -5.94 | -4.44 | 0.995-1.062 | Spearman >= 0.999; E[A] top-6 held in 23/24 |
| sensor drift (D) | 0.89-0.99 of the mean-equivalent bias | | | — | E[D] top-6 held in 6/8; E[A] in 8/8 |
| zero censoring (D) | -0.11 | -0.00 | +0.01 | — | top-3 unchanged |
| symmetric heterogeneity (D) | +0.11 | +0.02 | -0.06 | — | — |
| structured heterogeneity (D) | -1.55 | -1.89 | -1.65 | 0.995 | — |

Notes. (W) widening, a factor on the interval; (D) displacement, in baseline posterior standard deviations. Risk gives the whole-network Spearman rank correlation, then the top-6 Jaccard index under $\bar{P}$ / $E[A]$. Best fit is the smallest RMSE reachable anywhere in the candidate library under that perturbation, as a multiple of the realised observation-noise RMSE of the same draw, so a value near one means the perturbation is not visible in the aggregate residual.

Basis. Thirty noise realisations unless stated otherwise. AR(1) is a Fisher calculation. Sensor bias is 24 arms of 30, the maximum taken separately for each coefficient, so its three values come from different arms. Drift is 2 nodes x 4 endpoints. Zero censoring is 30 realisations, but the 10 floored readings of 294 census the reference seed alone. Symmetric heterogeneity is 25 fields; structured heterogeneity is one design and a single paired draw, whose median proxy-gap fraction over 30 draws is 0.86/1.12/0.92 (raw), with 5-95% intervals that overlap across zones.
